The residue of $14$ modulo $6$ is the integer $0\le r<6$ such that

$$
14≡r\,(\text{mod}\,6).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $14$ as an integer multiple of $6,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $14≡2\,(\text{mod}\,6)$ because

$$
14=2\cdot 6+2.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $14$ modulo $6$ is $2.$

**Method 2**

We can use the subtraction property:

$$
\begin{aligned}14 & ≡14-0 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡14-2\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡14-12 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $14$ modulo $6$ is $2.$
